snippet.title: India Has 40% Women Working… But Only 13% in Leadership? The Real Problem 🔥 #startup #business
snippet.description:
Summary:
India’s female workforce participation is rising, but women are still missing from leadership roles. This gap could impact India’s growth and future.

Full Description:
India has seen a rise in female labour force participation, reaching nearly 40% in 2025. However, when it comes to leadership roles, the number drops sharply — only 13% of leadership positions are held by women.

From IITs with just ~14% female faculty to corporate boards where 77% of companies have only 1–2 women directors, the leadership gap is real.

Globally, leaders like Indra Nooyi (PepsiCo), Mary Barra (General Motors), and Susan Wojcicki (YouTube) have proven that women-led organizations drive better performance and innovation.

This video explains:

Why women are missing from leadership roles in India
Key data and global comparisons
The real problem: lack of high-quality opportunities
Why this matters for India’s goal of becoming a developed nation by 2047

👉 India doesn’t lack talent — it lacks representation.

snippet.title: The Flying Tigers - America's Forgotten Heroes | Episode 3: Over the Hump | FD History
snippet.description:
The Flying Tigers - Episode 3: Over the Hump | History Documentary

Watch 'The Flying Tigers - Episode 4' here: https://youtu.be/qBxEgDTotJg

In this episode:
During World War II, the skies above the eastern Himalayas became the scene of one of the most dangerous air operations in aviation history. After Japanese forces cut off China's overland supply routes in 1942, Allied pilots were forced to fly vital fuel, weapons, and equipment over the towering mountain range known simply as "The Hump." Extreme weather, high winds, high-altitude conditions, and constant navigational challenges: crews faced enormous risks on every mission. So many aircraft were lost along the route that pilots nicknamed it "Aluminium Alley," claiming they could navigate by the wreckage scattered across the mountains below.

This documentary tells the remarkable story of the Hump Airlift, the pilots who kept China supplied during World War II, and the route that became one of the deadliest air corridors of the war.

The series:
During World War II, a legendary group of American fighter pilots became famous for defending China against Japanese air attacks. Known as the Flying Tigers, these US airmen operated from bases in western China and played a crucial role in the early air war in the Pacific.

Formed before the United States officially entered the war, the Flying Tigers fought against overwhelming odds and quickly earned a reputation for their daring tactics and fierce resistance. Some historians believe their growing presence in the Far East increased tensions with Japan and contributed to the chain of events that ultimately led to the attack on Attack on Pearl Harbor.

From December 1941 to June 1942, the Flying Tigers provided vital aerial defence for China during one of the darkest periods of the war. Their story is one of courage, sacrifice, and innovation — yet much of it has remained untold. Until now.

snippet.title: 'THEY LIED ABOUT TRUMP'
snippet.description:
I've been waiting 10 years to ask someone these questions, and today I finally get to do that.

Ever since I was a kid, I’ve been fascinated by American politics. Back then, I used to watch the elections, every interview and all the debates from my bedroom, trying to figure out why a system thousands of miles away felt so consequential to my life.

So when I was given the chance to have a sit-down conversation with Vice President Of The United States JD Vance, I knew I didn’t just want to ask him about headlines.

I wanted to understand the person behind the headlines.

At the start of the conversation, I said to him: “To understand the people that are sitting in front of me, you have to get a picture of their early context.”

And the reality is, I didn't truly know his context…

What I really wanted to find out by speaking with VP is: How much of what people think they know about VP Vance is ACTUALLY true?

Long before he entered the White House, VP grew up in a home shaped by addiction, poverty, instability, and a revolving door of father figures.

I went into this conversation wanting to understand how a kid raised in addiction and instability became the Vice President of the United States. And then get to the bottom of what he really thinks about everything happening in the world right now with no questions left unsaid.

We spoke about:

- The childhood instability that shaped the way he sees people.
- The conversation that changed his view of Donald Trump.
- His return to Christianity after years as an atheist.
- Whether he wants to be President one day.
- The immigration debate that is dividing America.
- Why doesn't he trust the UK Government?
- Whether he thinks aliens exist…
- When will a proposed ceasefire deal with Iran happen?
- Navigating one of the most demanding jobs on earth while raising a young family.

One of the things that I've come to learn is just try and meet everybody as I experience them.

Regardless of where you stand politically, this conversation goes deeper than politics.

And as a podcaster, having these conversations is important, as it goes beyond the headlines and shows you how the people in power actually think.

In the late 16th century, a wave of terror swept across Europe as thousands of women were tortured and burned at the stake with full backing from the Church. While France and Germany saw up to 40,000 executions, Britain remained largely untouched—until King James declared his own personal war on the occult. His 1597 treatise, Daemonology, served as a lethal blueprint for identifying and destroying witches, sparking a century of state-sponsored persecution. 

This film explores how James's obsession fueled trials across the country, while revealing groundbreaking archaeological evidence from Cornwall that suggests witchcraft wasn’t just a paranoid myth, but a practice that survived in the shadows for centuries.
